1.note: “Behold”, from “ἰδοὺ”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.
The Greek word (en) translated here as “in” could also be translated as “with” in some contexts.

3.note: NU reads, guilty of an eternal sin.

4.note: literally, a modion, a dry measuring basket containing about a peck (about 9 liters)

6.note: 200 denarii was about 7 or 8 months wages for an agricultural laborer.

7.note: Corban is a Hebrew word for an offering devoted to God.
NU ends Jesus’ direct quote and question after “latrine”, ending the verse with “Thus he declared all foods clean.

8.note: The word translated “generation” here (genea) could also be translated “people”, “race”, or “family”.

10.note: Rabboni is a transliteration of the Aramaic word for “great teacher.”

11.note: “Hosanna” means “save us” or “help us, we pray”.

12.note: literally, lepta (or widow’s mites). Lepta are very small brass coins worth half a quadrans each, which is a quarter of the copper assarion. Lepta are worth less than 1% of an agricultural worker’s daily wages.
A quadrans is a coin worth about 1/64 of a denarius. A denarius is about one day’s wages for an agricultural laborer.

13.note: The word translated “generation” (genea) could also be translated “race”, “family”, or “people”.

14.note: 300 denarii was about a year’s wages for an agricultural laborer.
Abba is a Greek spelling for the Aramaic word for “Father” or “Daddy” used in a familiar, respectful, and loving way.

16.note: One isolated manuscript omits verses 9-20 but adds this “short ending of Mark” to the end of verse 8: They told all that had been commanded them briefly to those around Peter. After that, Jesus himself sent them out, from east to west, with the sacred and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation.

NU includes the text of verses 9-20, but mentions in a footnote that a few manuscripts omitted it. The translators of the World English Bible regard Mark 16:9-20 as reliable based on an overwhelming majority of textual evidence, including not only the authoritative Greek Majority Text New Testament, but also the TR and many of the manuscripts cited in the NU text.
